entities.text:
High Court Of Madhya Pradesh
 At Gwalior
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: Shri Atul Gupta, Advocate for the appellant.
Shri A. K. Nirankari, Public Prosecutor for the State.
IA No. 1814/2024, application under Section 5 of Limitation Act is taken up, considered and for the reasons stated therein, is hereby allowed.
Also heard on I.A.No.1815/2024, first application for suspension of sentence and grant of bail moved on behalf of the appellant.

The trial Court has convicted the appellant under Section 366 of IPC and sentenced to five years RI with fine of Rs.5000/-; under Section 376(3) of IPC and sentenced to twenty years RI with fine of Rs.20000/-; and, under Section 3/4(2) of POCSO Act, and sentenced to twenty years RI with fine of Rs.10000/-, with default stipulation, vide judgment of conviction and order of sentence dated 23.06.2023 passed in Special Sessions Trial No. 31/2021 by Second Additional Sessions Judge & Special Judge (POCSO Act), Ganj Basoda, District Vidisha.

entities.text: Second Additional Sessions Judge & Special Judge (POCSO Act), Ganj Basoda
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: As per prosecution story, on 29.03.2021 complainant lodged a report at Police Station City Ganj Basoda, District Vidisha that some unknown person luring her minor daughter for marriage took her along with him.
On these allegations, FIR (Ex.P/9) was lodged against unknown person.
After registration of FIr the prosecutrix was recovered and statements of prosecutrix and her parents were recorded.
The appellant was arrested on 31.3.2021.
After completion of investigation challan was filed.
The case was committed to the Special Court.
Learned Special Judge after appreciation of evidence and  2 material available on record has convicted and sentenced the appellant as aforesaid.
Learned counsel for the appellant submits that appellant is innocent and has been falsely implicated in the crime.

The prosecutrix in her statements recorded under Sections 161 and 164 of CrPC as well as in the statement recorded before the Court below has deposed that she has married the appellant as well evident from para 21 of the impugned judgment.
Further, the prosecutrix herself has deposed in her statement that she was above 16 years of age at the time of commission of alleged crime.
The Court below has not appreciated the evidence in its right perspective.
The appellant has suffered jail incarceration for more than a year.
The appeal is of 2024.

There is no likelihood of hearing of Ravi vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 16 February, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/146015161/
1 appeal in near future.

entities.text: Ravi vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In view of aforesaid, learned counsel for the appellant prays for suspension of remaining jail sentence and grant of bail to the appellant.
Learned counsel for the respondent/State has opposed the prayer.

Upon hearing learned counsel for the parties, this Court refrains from commenting upon the rival contentions touching the merits of the case, however, in the obtaining facts and circumstances of the case and the fact that the prosecutrix has already married as also the fact that the appeal is of 2024,
there is no likelihood of hearing of appeal in near future, in the opinion of this Court the appellant is held entitled to get the benefit of suspension of jail sentence.
Accordingly, IA No.1815/2024, stands allowed and it is directed that the jail sentence of present appellant shall remain suspended during pendency of the present appeal and he shall be released on bail subject to verification of the factum of depositing the fine amount and on his furnishing a personal bond in the sum of Rs.1,50,000/- (Rupees One Lac Fifty Thousand only) with one solvent surety in the like amount to the satisfaction of the Trial Court.
Appellant is directed to appear before the Registry of this Court first on 22.05.2024 and on other subsequent dates as may be fixed in this behalf.
Observations on facts, if any, are only for the purpose of deciding the instant I.A. and shall have no bearing on the merits of the appeal.
Accordingly, the said IA stands allowed and disposed of.
Certified copy as per rules.

(ROHIT ARYA) (BINOD KUMAR DWIVEDI)
 JUDGE JUDGE yog  YOGESH  VERMA  2024.02.17  11:52:58  +05'30'
